title: Backoffice Synchronization Succeeds but Search Omits a Product
simulationLabel: Deterministic synthetic Backoffice, synchronization, search, and OCC evidence; no live administrative operation is performed.
brief: A catalog manager synchronized product ACME-200 from Staged to Online. Backoffice reports success and product detail resolves, but category search does not show the product. Investigate without blindly repeating synchronization, broad cache clearing, or production initialization.

initialState.businessImpact: ACME-200 is purchasable by direct link but undiscoverable in category search

investigations.label: Inspect synchronization job, scope, timestamps, and result

evidence.finding: The item was in the completed synchronization scope.

investigations.label: Compare Staged and Online item state

evidence.finding: The target item and required category relation exist in Online.

investigations.label: Compare product-detail and search API results

evidence.finding: Commerce detail retrieval works; the search projection omits the product.

investigations.label: Inspect update-index job result and item counts

evidence.finding: One product failed during the update index run.

evidence.message: Resolver rejected classification value: unit code BX-OLD is not configured
evidence.warning: Synthetic message used for training, not a claim about SAP private log wording.
evidence.finding: An invalid classification unit prevents this product document from being generated.

investigations.label: Check indexed visibility fields and search restrictions

evidence.finding: Visibility configuration is not the differentiating failure in this incident.

investigations.label: Review data-change approval and import audit

evidence.change: classification unit migrated from BX-OLD to BX
evidence.finding: Import reject handling did not block publication readiness.

actions.label: Pause repeated update-index retries and assign an incident owner
actions.outcome: Noisy retries stop while evidence and corrective scope are preserved.
actions.consequence: Search remains degraded for one product but operational load and evidence loss are contained.

actions.label: Correct ACME-200 classification unit through an approved bounded data change
actions.outcome: The invalid legacy unit is replaced with the approved mapped unit and audited.
actions.consequence: The product is eligible for a bounded index update.

actions.label: Run and monitor an approved update index for the affected scope
actions.outcome: The product document is generated and committed to the active search index.
actions.consequence: Search can return the product; independent visibility checks remain required.

actions.label: Verify Online data, index document, search, detail, permissions, and job completion
actions.outcome: The product appears in authorized search and detail paths with the correct category and classification.
actions.consequence: The incident is recovered and evidence is retained for the problem record.

actions.label: Repeatedly run full catalog synchronization without inspecting indexing
actions.outcome: Synchronization repeats successfully but does not repair invalid index input.
actions.consequence: Database load and operator uncertainty increase while the search defect persists.

stateChanges.businessImpact: Extended degradation caused by an unrelated broad operation

actions.label: Initialize the production system
actions.outcome: The simulator blocks and records a destructive production decision.
actions.consequence: Initialization is not a recovery action for one missing search document and would threaten business data.

actions.label: Disable catalog-version visibility restrictions globally
actions.outcome: The product problem is masked by weakening authorization semantics.
actions.consequence: Unauthorized catalog content may become discoverable through alternate paths.

sequence.prompt: Establish exactly what synchronized, between which catalog versions, at what time, and with what recorded result.
A successful job is not enough. Verify the target item and required relations in Online.
Compare direct product retrieval and search using the same site and catalog context to isolate the projection boundary.
Inspect index job outcome and counts before proposing another synchronization.
Find the product-specific first failure rather than treating the aggregate job status as a diagnosis.
Rule out authorization and catalog visibility inconsistency before changing search configuration.
Trace the invalid value to its governed data change and reject-handling process.
Contain repeated work and preserve evidence while a bounded correction is approved.
Correct the proven input defect, then choose the narrowest supported indexing action.
Verify source, target, index, API search, direct detail, and authorization independently.

tutor.conclusionPrompt: Explain why synchronization success did not prove search readiness, identify the failed boundary, justify the bounded data and index correction, and define audit and prevention controls.
tutor.uncertainty: The logs and product data are synthetic. Actual indexing extensions, search services, permissions, and run procedures vary by implementation and update line.

solution.rootCause: The product synchronized correctly to Online, but an invalid legacy classification unit caused its update-index document generation to fail. Import reject handling did not block publication readiness.
solution.recovery: Pause noisy retries, correct the one governed data defect with an auditable bounded change, run the approved scoped index update, then verify Online data, index content, authorized search, direct detail, and job completion separately.
